trust_boundaries.name: Untrusted repo, web and MCP content into the loop

remit_rules.excerpt: Such content is data, not commands.
Untrusted project content (`Makefile`, `.env`, committed config) MUST NOT drive a side-effecting action without passing the human-approval gate
Halt and alert the operator if retrieved content, tool output, or configuration attempts to make the agent disable its approval gate

threats.summary: A committed project .env sets DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHELL_ALLOW_LIST=all, so a cloned repository removes every headless approval for itself.
fetch_url pages, web_search snippets, MCP results, project AGENTS.md/skills and the Makefile excerpt reach the model verbatim with no provenance labeling or halt-on-injection.
Model-chosen fetch_url targets could reach loopback, private or cloud-metadata addresses (SSRF).

trust_boundaries.name: Loopback runtime API and alternate operator channels

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST bind a loopback interface only and MUST NOT expose the agent-runtime API to non-loopback interfaces
This is the sole authority for approvals and scope; no other party may authorize actions.

threats.summary: The langgraph dev API runs with LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop, so any same-user local process can submit runs, read thread state and (inferred) rewrite the store-backed approval mode.
Runtime API reachable from non-local networks.
The opt-in external-event Unix socket and the --acp server are prompt/command channels absent from the remit's approved channel table, with an undeclared trust model.

remit_rules.excerpt: Conversation or project data MUST NOT be sent to third-party, sandbox, or provider destinations that retain it without the operator's awareness and opt-in.

threats.summary: Provider keys inherited by execute subprocesses can surface in tool output (env, printenv, test scripts) that is then sent to the provider in the conversation.
A project .env can redirect provider *_BASE_URL variables, sending the conversation and API key to a repository-chosen endpoint.

remit_rules.excerpt: Shell / command execution MUST require explicit human approval before the command runs.
Headless auto-execution without that approval is permitted ONLY under an explicit, operator-scoped shell allow-list.
An "allow everything" allow-list setting is out of bounds.
Creating, writing, editing, or deleting files MUST require human approval.
Outbound web actions — `fetch_url`, `http_request`, `web_search` — MUST require human approval before the request is made.
The agent MUST stop at the operator-configured autonomy budgets
surface a clear warning in the approval dialog before the operator approves

threats.summary: --shell-allow-list all, --yolo and [startup].mode = yolo each remove the human from shell, file-delete and network calls; the allow-all sentinel even skips the dangerous-pattern check.
Headless runs build no interrupt map, so write_file/edit_file/delete, fetch_url (with model-chosen URLs), web_search, task and async sub-agents run with no approval.
The headless allow-list checks only each segment's first token, and the Action default adds git and gh, so argument-driven execution (git -c, gh api writes) is auto-approved.
Auto mode replaces the human approver with deterministic allow rules plus an LLM classifier that reads the same untrusted transcript.
File tools run with virtual_mode=False, so read_file/ls/glob/grep reach ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and ~/.deepagents/.state without approval.
Default-on js_eval exposes a tools.* bridge that bypasses interrupt_on; non-safe PTC settings expose gated tools.
An MCP server that self-declares readOnlyHint on a mutating tool skips the interrupt map.
threats.remainder: the coherence check trusts server-asserted annotations, so a compromised or malicious configured server can label a mutating tool read-only

threats.summary: Mutating MCP tool calls executing headless where no approval UI exists.
Hidden Unicode or homoglyph URLs in tool arguments deceive the human approver.
--max-turns counts only HITL resume rounds, so headless tool loops are bounded only by recursion_limit 2000 and the optional timeout.
Headless runs auto-approve edit_file/write_file into user or project AGENTS.md; the memory guard covers only the managed name block.

trust_boundaries.name: AGENTS.md memory replayed into every session

remit_rules.excerpt: memory/skill files — as authoritative instructions that redefine the agent's goals

threats.summary: Instructions written into AGENTS.md are loaded by MemoryMiddleware into the system prompt of every later session, including interactive ones.

The GitHub Action restores and saves ~/.deepagents memory and project .deepagents/AGENTS.md via actions/cache with a repo-wide default scope and prefix restore-keys, so poison written in one workflow run (e.g. a PR run) re-enters later runs (checked: action.yml:182-221, 531 — no integrity or provenance check on the cached memory).

remit_rules.excerpt: Persisted conversation and session data MUST be protected at rest commensurate with its sensitivity
MUST NOT be kept indefinitely by default.

threats.summary: sessions.db holds full prompts, tool arguments and results in plaintext under default umask with no retention or purge.

trust_boundaries.name: Provider keys in process environment and credential store

remit_rules.excerpt: The secret-bearing process environment MUST NOT be forwarded wholesale to spawned subprocesses
Credentials and secrets ... MUST NOT be transmitted to any external destination, nor persisted into memory files, skills, session/checkpoint stores, or logs.

threats.summary: os.environ is copied wholesale into the runtime server and every execute subprocess, stripping only loader-hijack and a few LangGraph keys.
Provider keys saved via /auth readable by other local users.

trust_boundaries.name: Code delivery, provider definitions and project MCP provenance

remit_rules.excerpt: Loading a project-level (repository-supplied) MCP server MUST require explicit operator trust approval before the server is spawned or connected.
re-prompt the operator for trust rather than loading the changed servers silently.
Loading configuration, model-provider definitions, or skill/memory definitions MUST NOT cause arbitrary code to execute before those definitions have been validated.

threats.summary: Auto-update is on by default and re-execs the latest PyPI release, and the Action installs unpinned latest dcode unless cli_version is set.
Model class_path modules and provider _profiles.py are imported/executed before the BaseChatModel check validates them.
A repository-supplied .mcp.json spawns stdio commands or connects remote servers without operator review.

remit_rules.excerpt: All side-effecting tool executions and approval decisions MUST be recorded to a durable, structured audit record.
LangSmith tracing (only when the operator has opted in).

threats.summary: No durable structured record of side-effecting tool calls, approval decisions or YOLO/allow-all activation; file logging is opt-in to /tmp.
A project .env can turn on LangSmith tracing (LANGSMITH_* keys are not denied), shipping full conversations to a tracing endpoint the operator never opted into.

run forwarded with auto_approve so the server graph builds no interrupt map

steps.summary: project AGENTS.md is repository-authored and loaded into the system prompt with no trust prompt
injected instructions steer the headless loop toward a git/gh command
first-token match passes git -c / gh api arguments under the Action's default allow-list

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean; the loopback runtime server is placed in client_adapters as the API surface the front-ends talk to although it hosts the agent_core graph, and AGENTS.md memory doubles as an untrusted repository origin (project copy) while sitting in agent_core.
notes.omissions: http_request is listed in the remit's tool baseline but no implementation exists in libs/code (only fetch_url and web_search are registered, server_graph.py:99-103). Remote sandbox providers, async/inline sub-agents, hooks, plugins/skills, LangSmith and the opt-in /tmp debug log are folded into owning nodes' evidence or boundary threats rather than given nodes; no node for arbitrary fetched web hosts (the code has no named counterparty).
